The graph above shows the curve $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ and the line $y=1.$

The **exact** value of the $x$-coordinate of the point $A$ is 
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The $y$-values of both functions are the same at the intersection point. Equating the two equations gives:

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=1
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1)=\frac{\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

This value lies outside $-\frac{3\pi }{2}<x<-\frac{\pi }{2}.$ To get a value that's inside the required domain, we add $-\pi $ to the principal value. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =x+(-\pi ) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}-\pi  \\  & =-\frac{3\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the $x$-coordinate of $A$ is $-\frac{3\pi }{4}.$
